strategy_description: Increasing num_warps from 8 to 16 in register-constrained kernels worsens scheduler utilization instead of improving it. The change reduced eligible warps per scheduler from 1.4 to 1.19 and increased scheduler idle cycles from 40.1% to 48.5%, causing 2.18x slowdown. This occurs because higher warp counts hit occupancy limits, creating more contention for limited resources.
slow_pseudocode:
kernel_launch(
  num_warps=8,  # 256 threads per block
  registers_per_thread=125
)
fast_pseudocode:
kernel_launch(
  num_warps=16, # 512 threads per block
  registers_per_thread=95
)
applicable_when: Scheduler Statistics.No Eligible > 35% AND Occupancy.Block Limit Registers <= 2 AND registers_per_thread > 90
do_not_apply_when: Kernel already register-limited (Block Limit Registers <= 1) or when increasing num_warps would exceed register capacity per SM
framework_notes: Triton num_warps parameter controls thread block size. Equivalent to CUDA blockDim.x = num_warps * 32. Register pressure increases with warp count.

strategy_title: Avoid aggressive tile size reduction for occupancy
strategy_description: Reducing tile sizes from BLOCK_M=128,BLOCK_N=64 to BLOCK_M=64,BLOCK_N=32 decreased registers per thread from 125 to 76 and increased theoretical occupancy from 25% to 37.5%, but caused 2.15x performance regression. The duration increased from 299.71μs to 644.45μs despite higher occupancy and more eligible warps per scheduler (1.4→2.14). The doubled grid size (1024→2048) created excessive kernel launch overhead and reduced arithmetic intensity per block.
slow_pseudocode:
BLOCK_M = 64
BLOCK_N = 32
grid = (cdiv(seq_len, BLOCK_M), batch * n_heads)
# More blocks, less work per block
fast_pseudocode:
BLOCK_M = 128
BLOCK_N = 64
grid = (cdiv(seq_len, BLOCK_M), batch * n_heads)
# Fewer blocks, more work per block
applicable_when: Theoretical Occupancy is below 40% and registers per thread exceed 100, but kernel duration is already reasonable (<500μs)
do_not_apply_when: Current performance is acceptable, or when reducing tile sizes would double grid size and create launch overhead that exceeds occupancy benefits
framework_notes: Triton: BLOCK_M and BLOCK_N are compile-time constants that determine register allocation and grid dimensions
